title: Universal property of a power series ring mapping into a complete ring
statement: Let $\Lambda$ and $T$ be commutative rings, $\mathfrak a\subseteq T$ an ideal such that $T$ is $\mathfrak a$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], $\alpha:\Lambda\to T$ a ring homomorphism, $n\ge0$, and $t_1,\ldots,t_n\in\mathfrak a$. Write $t^E=t_1^{e_1}\cdots t_n^{e_n}$ and $|E|=e_1+\cdots+e_n$ for $E\in\mathbf N^n$. Then there is a ring homomorphism $\Phi:\Lambda[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]\to T$ from the formal power series ring [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] such that $\Phi(\lambda)=\alpha(\lambda)$ for $\lambda\in\Lambda$ (constant series) and $\Phi(x_i)=t_i$ for $i=1,\ldots,n$; for $F=\sum_Ea_Ex^E$, $\Phi(F)$ is the unique element of $T$ with $\Phi(F)\equiv\sum_{|E|<m}\alpha(a_E)t^E\pmod{\mathfrak a^m}$ for every $m\ge1$. Moreover $\Phi$ is the only ring homomorphism $\Lambda[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]\to T$ which agrees with $\alpha$ on $\Lambda$ and sends $x_i$ to $t_i$ for every $i$.

source.place: used without statement as 'the universal property of power series rings' in More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07NL (lemma-power-series-ring-over-Cohen-fs, line 9719), in the proof of Lemma Tag 07NN (lemma-embed-map-Noetherian-complete-local-rings, line 9812: the map phi' : Lambda[[x]] -> S[[y]], x_i -> phi(x_i) + y_i) and in Algebra, proof of Theorem Tag 032A (algebra.tex line 45014: Lambda[[x_1..x_n]] -> R, x_i -> y_i); agent-formulated

proof.text: *Notation and partial sums.* By [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] an element of $\Lambda[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$ is a family $F=(a_E)_{E\in\mathbf N^n}$ of elements of $\Lambda$, written $\sum_Ea_Ex^E$, with coefficientwise sum and product $(FG)_H=\sum_{E+E'=H}a_Eb_{E'}$ for $G=(b_{E'})$; a constant $\lambda\in\Lambda$ is the series $\lambda x^0$, and $x_i$ is the series with coefficient $1$ at the $i$-th unit vector $\varepsilon_i$ and $0$ elsewhere, so that $x^E=x_1^{e_1}\cdots x_n^{e_n}$ is the series with coefficient $1$ at $E$ and $0$ elsewhere, and $a_Ex^E$ (product of the constant $a_E$ with $x^E$) is the series with coefficient $a_E$ at $E$ and $0$ elsewhere. For $F=\sum_Ea_Ex^E$ and $m\ge1$ put $P_m(F)=\sum_{|E|<m}\alpha(a_E)t^E\in T$, a finite sum (there are finitely many $E\in\mathbf N^n$ with $|E|<m$). Since $t_i\in\mathfrak a$, $t^E\in\mathfrak a^{|E|}$ for every $E$. Hence for $m'\ge m\ge1$, $P_{m'}(F)-P_m(F)=\sum_{m\le|E|<m'}\alpha(a_E)t^E\in\mathfrak a^m$.

source.place: fact used without statement or proof in the proof of Lemma Tag 07NL (line 9719); proof written by an agent

proof.text: *Definition of $\Phi(F)$, and its characterization.* By [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] the canonical map $T\to\varprojlim_mT/\mathfrak a^m$, $s\mapsto(s\bmod\mathfrak a^m)_m$, is bijective. By step 1 the classes $P_m(F)\bmod\mathfrak a^m$ form a compatible family: the image of $P_{m+1}(F)\bmod\mathfrak a^{m+1}$ under $T/\mathfrak a^{m+1}\to T/\mathfrak a^m$ is $P_{m+1}(F)\bmod\mathfrak a^m=P_m(F)\bmod\mathfrak a^m$. By surjectivity there is $\Phi(F)\in T$ with $\Phi(F)\equiv P_m(F)\pmod{\mathfrak a^m}$ for every $m\ge1$; by injectivity it is the only such element (two such elements have the same image in the inverse limit). In particular, an element $s\in T$ with $s\in\mathfrak a^m$ for every $m\ge1$ is $0$ (it and $0$ have the same image), i.e. $\bigcap_m\mathfrak a^m=0$. This defines a map $\Phi:\Lambda[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]\to T$ and proves the clause of the statement that $\Phi(F)$ is the unique element congruent to $\sum_{|E|<m}\alpha(a_E)t^E$ modulo $\mathfrak a^m$ for all $m\ge1$.

source.place: fact used without statement or proof in the proof of Lemma Tag 07NL (line 9719); proof written by an agent

proof.text: *$\Phi$ is a ring homomorphism.* Fix $m\ge1$ and $F=\sum a_Ex^E$, $G=\sum b_Ex^E$. (a) Sums are coefficientwise, so $P_m(F+G)=P_m(F)+P_m(G)$ as $\alpha$ is additive; hence $\Phi(F+G)$ and $\Phi(F)+\Phi(G)$ are both congruent to $P_m(F+G)$ modulo $\mathfrak a^m$ for every $m$, and they are equal by the uniqueness of step 2. (b) The unit $1=x^0$ has $P_m(1)=\alpha(1)t^0=1$ for every $m\ge1$, so $\Phi(1)=1$ by step 2. (c) $P_m(F)P_m(G)=\sum_{|E|<m,\,|E'|<m}\alpha(a_E)\alpha(b_{E'})t^{E+E'}$. If $|E+E'|<m$ then $|E|,|E'|<m$, so the terms with $|E+E'|<m$ are all present and, grouped by $H=E+E'$, give $\sum_{|H|<m}\alpha\bigl(\sum_{E+E'=H}a_Eb_{E'}\bigr)t^H=P_m(FG)$ ($\alpha$ is a ring homomorphism); the remaining terms have $|E+E'|\ge m$ and lie in $\mathfrak a^m$ (step 1). So $P_m(F)P_m(G)\equiv P_m(FG)\pmod{\mathfrak a^m}$. Since $\Phi(F)-P_m(F)$ and $\Phi(G)-P_m(G)$ lie in the ideal $\mathfrak a^m$, also $\Phi(F)\Phi(G)\equiv P_m(F)P_m(G)\equiv P_m(FG)\pmod{\mathfrak a^m}$, for every $m\ge1$; by the uniqueness of step 2, $\Phi(FG)=\Phi(F)\Phi(G)$.

source.place: fact used without statement or proof in the proof of Lemma Tag 07NL (line 9719); proof written by an agent

proof.text: *The values on $\Lambda$ and on the $x_i$.* For $\lambda\in\Lambda$ the series $\lambda x^0$ has $P_m(\lambda)=\alpha(\lambda)$ for every $m\ge1$, so $\Phi(\lambda)=\alpha(\lambda)$ by step 2. For the series $x_i$ (coefficient $1$ at $\varepsilon_i$, $|\varepsilon_i|=1$) one has $P_1(x_i)=0$ and $P_m(x_i)=t_i$ for $m\ge2$; as $t_i\in\mathfrak a$, $t_i\equiv P_m(x_i)\pmod{\mathfrak a^m}$ for every $m\ge1$, so $\Phi(x_i)=t_i$ by step 2. (For $n=0$ there are no $x_i$ and $\Phi=\alpha$.) With step 3 this proves the existence part of the statement.

source.place: fact used without statement or proof in the proof of Lemma Tag 07NL (line 9719); proof written by an agent

proof.text: *Series without terms of degree $<m$ lie in the ideal generated by the monomials of degree $m$.* Let $m\ge1$ and $R=\sum_Gr_Gx^G\in\Lambda[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$ with $r_G=0$ for $|G|<m$. Let $\mathcal E_m=\{E\in\mathbf N^n:|E|=m\}$, a finite set. For each $G$ with $|G|\ge m$ choose $E(G)\in\mathcal E_m$ with $E(G)\le G$ componentwise (lower the entries of $G$ one unit at a time, from the last nonzero entry, until the total is $m$). For $E\in\mathcal E_m$ let $g_E\in\Lambda[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$ have coefficient $r_{E+H}$ at $H$ if $|E+H|\ge m$ and $E(E+H)=E$, and $0$ otherwise. By the product formula of [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] the coefficient of $x^Eg_E$ at $G$ is $0$ unless $E\le G$, and then it is the coefficient of $g_E$ at $G-E$, namely $r_G$ if $E(G)=E$ and $0$ otherwise (note $|G|\ge|E|=m$ when $E\le G$). Summing over the finite set $\mathcal E_m$, the coefficient of $\sum_{E\in\mathcal E_m}x^Eg_E$ at $G$ is $r_G$ if $|G|\ge m$ (exactly one $E$, namely $E(G)$, contributes) and $0=r_G$ if $|G|<m$ (no $E\in\mathcal E_m$ is $\le G$). Hence $R=\sum_{E\in\mathcal E_m}x^Eg_E$, a finite sum.

source.place: fact used without statement or proof in the proof of Lemma Tag 07NL (line 9719); proof written by an agent

proof.text: *Uniqueness among all ring homomorphisms.* Let $\Phi':\Lambda[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]\to T$ be any ring homomorphism with $\Phi'(\lambda)=\alpha(\lambda)$ for $\lambda\in\Lambda$ and $\Phi'(x_i)=t_i$ for all $i$ (no continuity is assumed). Then $\Phi'(x^E)=t^E$ by multiplicativity. Fix $F=\sum a_Ex^E$ and $m\ge1$, and write $F=F_{<m}+R$ with $F_{<m}=\sum_{|E|<m}a_Ex^E$ (a finite sum of the series $a_Ex^E=a_E\cdot x^E$ of step 1) and $R=F-F_{<m}$, whose coefficients vanish in degrees $<m$. Then $\Phi'(F_{<m})=\sum_{|E|<m}\alpha(a_E)t^E=P_m(F)$. By step 5, $R=\sum_{|E|=m}x^Eg_E$, so $\Phi'(R)=\sum_{|E|=m}t^E\Phi'(g_E)\in\mathfrak a^m$ since $t^E\in\mathfrak a^m$ (step 1). Hence $\Phi'(F)\equiv P_m(F)\pmod{\mathfrak a^m}$ for every $m\ge1$, and $\Phi'(F)=\Phi(F)$ by the uniqueness in step 2. So $\Phi'=\Phi$.
